name: Regulatory intensity

subjectOf.text: Regulatory intensity is never constant: it increases after a market crash and then wanes as society and the market return to normalcy.
subjectOf.abstract: The phrase "regulatory sine curve," means: "that (1) regulatory intensity is never constant, but rather increases after a market crash, and then wanes as (and to the extent that) society and the market return to normalcy
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: In the absence of crises the intensity of regulation diminishes, because regulators cannot commit to long-term regulatory strategies and instead fall back on private strategies such as self-regulation to overcome resource constraints.
subjectOf.abstract: In the absence of crises, however, the intensity of regulation diminishes because regulators are unable to commit to long-term regulatory strategies and instead use private strategies like self-regulation to overcome resource constraints.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Dynamic Regulation of the Financial Services Industry (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2273857

subjectOf.text: Information generated by contingent capital securities may allow regulators to adjust their regulatory requirements and the intensity of regulatory investigations anticipatorily rather than after the fact.
subjectOf.abstract: Such information may allow regulators to anticipatorily adjust their regulatory requirements and the intensity of regulatory investigations.60
